name: iCIMS
notes: PARTIALLY VERIFIED, and the unverified part is most of the form.
Confirmed against a live iCIMS tenant on 19 Sep 2026:
- The entire application renders inside <iframe id='icims_content_iframe'>,
pointing at the same host with ?in_iframe=1. applyr only reaches it because
the manifest sets all_frames; without that there is nothing to fill.
- The application opens on a two-field step titled 'Enter Your Information':
input[name='css_loginName'] (email) and input[name='accept_privacy'] (consent),
submitted with #enterEmailSubmitButton. Those two selectors are real.
- The page carries an hCaptcha, rendered as a real <textarea> named
h-captcha-response. The detector ignores captcha controls, so it is never
filled - see isIgnored() in content/detector.js.
- Form fields use a css_ prefix. That convention is confirmed; the individual
names below are NOT.
NOT verified: everything after the email step. iCIMS requires an account before
the application form renders, so the personal-information, resume and EEO pages
have not been seen by this code. The css_* selectors below follow iCIMS's naming
convention and cannot mis-map - an exact name that does not exist simply does not
match - but expect to correct them on a first real application. Generic mode
carries these pages in the meantime; iCIMS labels its fields properly, which is
what generic mode needs.
About accept_privacy: this is a consent checkbox, and applyr only ticks it when
the user has set privacy_consent to yes in their own profile. It is their saved
answer, not an assumption - but it is worth knowing that it gets filled.
submit is empty on purpose. The email step's button is not an application
submission, and iCIMS spreads the real submit across later pages, so matching a
button here would log an application that was never sent.
